meta.actor: Claude — consolidation pass (no research, no content rewriting)
meta.scope: Every Grok batch file for Japan merged into one file. Records are byte-faithful to the batches except for the normalisations listed in _consolidation.

reports.title: Statistics Act (Act No. 53 of 2007) — 統計法
reports.publisher: National Diet of Japan / Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications (MIC)
reports.description: Foundational statute that comprehensively reformed Japan’s official statistics system. Defines official statistics as information infrastructure, establishes fundamental statistics (基幹統計) and fundamental statistical surveys, creates the Statistics Commission, requires a Master Plan concerning the Development of Official Statistics, and sets rules for statistical surveys, confidentiality, secondary use, and coordination across the highly decentralised Japanese statistical system. Replaced the 1947 Statistics Act.
reports._notes:
Prime static + recurring-citation node — direct analogue of Mexico’s LSNIEG and Argentina’s Ley 17.622.

Article 1 states the purpose: ‘to promote systematic and efficient development of official statistics and to ensure the usefulness thereof through specifying basic matters concerning the production and provision of official statistics, and thereby to contribute to sound development of the national economy and enhancement of the living standards of the citizens.’

Official statistics are explicitly recognised as ‘information infrastructure’ usable not only by administration but by society as a whole. Fundamental statistics include the Population Census statistics, National Accounts, and other statistics designated by the Minister of Internal Affairs and Communications. Every subsequent methodological document, survey approval, and quality report cites the 2007 Act as the legal foundation. No independent publication cadence is required; continuous institutional citation satisfies the expanded node definition.
_referenced_by: All fundamental statistical survey methodologies and implementation plans
Master Plan Concerning the Development of Official Statistics (Cabinet decision)
Statistics Commission deliberations and annual reports
MIC Director-General for Policy Planning (Statistical Policy) institutional documents
IMF SDDS / DQAF assessments of Japanese statistics
OECD reviews of the Japanese statistical system

reports.title: Statistics Bureau of Japan (SBJ) / 総務省統計局 — Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications
reports.publisher: Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications (MIC)
reports.description: Central statistical office responsible for producing many of Japan’s fundamental statistics (Population Census, Labour Force Survey, CPI, Family Income and Expenditure Survey, Economic Census, etc.) and for cross-governmental coordination of the decentralised official statistical system under the Statistics Act. Works with the National Statistics Center (NSTAC) for data processing and the Statistics Commission for oversight.
reports._notes: Institutional framework node. Japan’s statistical system is highly decentralised by international standards; SBJ plays the dual role of major producer and coordinator. Continuously referenced as the lead agency for fundamental statistics and for the e-Stat portal.
_referenced_by: Statistics Act and Master Plan
All SBJ survey methodological notes and press releases
e-Stat portal documentation
Cabinet Office National Accounts source documentation
International statistical assessments (IMF, OECD, UNSD)

reports.title: Population Census of Japan (国勢調査 / Kokusei Chōsa)
reports.publisher: Statistics Bureau of Japan (SBJ), Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications
reports.description: Quinquennial complete enumeration of the population and households of Japan. Provides the benchmark for population estimates, sampling frames for virtually all household surveys, and the demographic base for national accounts, labour force, and many other statistics. Conducted every five years since 1920 (with wartime interruption). The 2020 Census was the 21st; the 2025 Census (22nd) results are emerging.
reports._notes: Fundamental statistics under the Statistics Act. Serves as the primary sampling frame and population control totals for the Labour Force Survey, Family Income and Expenditure Survey, and many other programmes. Results feed directly into Population Estimates, National Accounts employment and household sector accounts, and prefectural accounts. 2020 Census total population: approximately 126.2 million; 2025 preliminary figures show continued decline.

reports.title: Consumer Price Index (CPI) / 消費者物価指数
reports.publisher: Statistics Bureau of Japan (SBJ)
reports.description: Monthly measure of the average change in prices of goods and services purchased by households throughout Japan. 2020-base index currently in use. Covers all Japan and major regions/cities; also publishes Tokyo-area early indicators. Core and other analytical series released.
reports._notes: Fundamental statistics. Compiled primarily from the Retail Price Survey. Widely used for inflation targeting discussions, real wage calculations, national accounts deflation, and poverty/income analysis. June 2026: +1.7% year-on-year. Disseminated under SDDS.

reports.title: Labour Force Survey (労働力調査)
reports.publisher: Statistics Bureau of Japan (SBJ)
reports.description: Monthly household survey providing official unemployment rate, labour force participation, employment by industry/occupation, hours worked, and related labour market indicators for persons aged 15 and over. Basic Tabulation monthly; Detailed Tabulation quarterly.
reports._notes: Fundamental statistics and primary source for the official unemployment rate (June 2026 seasonally adjusted: 2.5%). Sampling frame derived from Population Census. Results feed into National Accounts employment and compensation estimates, and are continuously cited in BOJ and Cabinet Office economic assessments.

reports.title: Family Income and Expenditure Survey (家計調査 / Kakei Chōsa)
reports.publisher: Statistics Bureau of Japan (SBJ)
reports.description: Monthly survey of household income, expenditure, savings and debt for two-or-more-person households (and separately for one-person and total households). Provides detailed consumption structure data used for CPI weights, national accounts private consumption estimates, and living-standards analysis.
reports._notes: Fundamental statistics. Core input into CPI basket weights and into the expenditure-side estimates of GDP. June 2026 real consumption expenditures for two-or-more-person households: −3.3% year-on-year. Complements the quinquennial National Survey of Family Income, Consumption and Wealth.

reports.title: Japanese System of National Accounts (JSNA) / 国民経済計算 — Annual Report and Quarterly Estimates
reports.publisher: Economic and Social Research Institute (ESRI), Cabinet Office
reports.description: Full system of national accounts compiled in accordance with the 2008 SNA (benchmark year currently 2020). Produces GDP by production, expenditure and income approaches, institutional sector accounts, supply-use tables, capital stock, and related aggregates. Quarterly preliminary estimates (QE) and annual report.
reports._notes: Fundamental statistics under the Statistics Act (explicitly listed). Compiled by the Department of National Accounts of ESRI. Draws heavily on SBJ source statistics (Population Census, Economic Census, Labour Force Survey, Family Income and Expenditure Survey, CPI, etc.), Ministry of Finance data, and BOJ financial statistics. Benchmark revisions approximately every five years incorporate new Input-Output tables and census results. 2008 SNA introduced in 2016; current benchmark year 2020.

reports.title: Economic Census (経済センサス) — Business Frame and Business Activity
reports.publisher: Statistics Bureau of Japan (SBJ) in cooperation with Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI)
reports.description: Large-scale census of establishments and enterprises providing the statistical business register (JSBR) frame and detailed economic activity data. Conducted periodically (Economic Census for Business Frame and for Business Activity). Foundation for annual and monthly business surveys and for national accounts production estimates.
reports._notes: Fundamental statistics. Provides the sampling frame and structural benchmarks for the Annual Business Survey, Monthly Survey on Service Industries, and many METI industrial statistics. Critical input into National Accounts production-side estimates and the statistical business register maintained with NSTAC profiling support for large enterprises.

reports.title: Monetary Base Statistics / マネタリーベース
reports.publisher: Bank of Japan (BOJ) — Research and Statistics Department
reports.description: Monthly statistics on the monetary base (banknotes in circulation + coins in circulation + current account balances at the Bank of Japan). Published with average amounts outstanding, end-of-period figures, and year-on-year growth rates. Key indicator of the stance of monetary policy and liquidity conditions.
reports._notes: Core high-frequency monetary aggregate. Continuously cited in BOJ monetary policy statements, Outlook for Economic Activity and Prices, and market analysis. May 2026 data show continued contraction in year-on-year growth consistent with the post-YCC normalisation phase. Complements the broader Monetary Base and the Bank of Japan’s Transactions series.

reports.title: Flow of Funds Accounts (FFA) / 資金循環統計
reports.publisher: Bank of Japan (BOJ) — Research and Statistics Department
reports.description: Quarterly integrated accounts of financial assets and liabilities by institutional sector (households, non-financial corporations, financial institutions, general government, central bank, overseas). Provides from-whom-to-whom matrices for major instruments and is a key input into national accounts financial accounts and stock estimates.
reports._notes: Major BOJ statistical product. Retroactively revised annually to incorporate new source data and methodological improvements. Directly used in the compilation of the financial accounts of the JSNA and in analyses of household and corporate balance-sheet adjustment. Q1 2026 preliminary figures released June 2026.

reports.title: Balance of Payments and International Investment Position (BPM6) / 国際収支統計・対外資産負債残高
reports.publisher: Ministry of Finance (MOF) and Bank of Japan (jointly)
reports.description: Monthly and quarterly balance-of-payments statistics and annual international investment position compiled according to the IMF’s BPM6. Covers current account, capital account, financial account, and external assets/liabilities. Detailed breakdowns by partner economy, industry (for direct investment), and currency available.
reports._notes: Compiled by the Bank of Japan under entrustment from the Minister of Finance pursuant to the Foreign Exchange and Foreign Trade Act. Core SDDS data category. Continuously referenced in MOF and BOJ economic reports, national accounts rest-of-world accounts, and international comparisons. Data from January 2014 onward on BPM6 basis.

reports.title: e-Stat — Portal Site of Official Statistics of Japan
reports.publisher: Statistics Bureau of Japan / National Statistics Center (NSTAC)
reports.description: Central government statistical data portal providing unified access to statistics produced by all ministries and agencies. Includes API access, visualisation tools, release calendars, and the full catalogue of official statistics. Primary dissemination channel for SBJ and many other producers.
reports._notes: Institutional dissemination infrastructure node. While not a statistical series itself, it is the load-bearing public face of the official statistical system and is continuously cited as the authoritative source for Japanese government statistics. Supports the secondary-use provisions of the Statistics Act.
_referenced_by: All major statistical release announcements
SBJ and ministry methodological documentation
Research and secondary-use applications
International data users and API consumers

reports.title: Retail Price Survey (小売物価統計調査) — Trend Survey and Structure Survey
reports.publisher: Statistics Bureau of Japan (SBJ)
reports.description: Monthly (Trend) and periodic (Structure) survey collecting retail prices of goods and services, house rents, and related charges at outlets across Japan. Primary data source for the Consumer Price Index. Also publishes retail prices of major items for Ku-area of Tokyo and nationwide uniform prices/charges.
reports._notes: Fundamental statistics / core input to CPI. Monthly Trend Survey provides the price observations used to compute the CPI; Structure Survey supplies weights and detailed outlet information. Continuously referenced in CPI methodology and annual reports. Tokyo-area early indicators are widely watched by markets.

reports.title: Employment Status Survey (就業構造基本調査 / Shūgyō Kōzō Kihon Chōsa)
reports.publisher: Statistics Bureau of Japan (SBJ)
reports.description: Quinquennial large-scale household survey providing detailed structural data on employment and unemployment status, type of employment, occupation, industry, working hours, income, and reasons for non-participation. Complements the monthly Labour Force Survey with richer cross-sectional detail at national and regional levels.
reports._notes: Fundamental statistics under the Statistics Act. Conducted every five years (most recent full results from 2022). Sampling based on Population Census enumeration districts. Results used for employment policy design, academic research, and as structural benchmarks that inform interpretation of the monthly LFS. Detailed regional tables support prefectural labour analysis.

reports.title: Housing and Land Survey (住宅・土地統計調査)
reports.publisher: Statistics Bureau of Japan (SBJ)
reports.description: Quinquennial survey of dwellings, households, and land ownership/use. Provides detailed statistics on housing stock, tenure, construction materials, facilities, residential land, and related living conditions. Fundamental statistics used for housing policy, urban planning, and as a structural input to national accounts dwelling services estimates.
reports._notes: Fundamental statistics. Latest major results from the 2023 survey. Complements the Population Census with specialised housing and land detail. Data feed into imputed rent calculations in the national accounts and into regional planning indicators.

reports.title: Monthly Labour Survey (毎月勤労統計調査 / Maitsuki Kinrō Tōkei Chōsa)
reports.publisher: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW)
reports.description: Monthly establishment survey of employment, wages (cash earnings, scheduled and non-scheduled), and hours worked for establishments with 5 or more employees (national and prefectural surveys) plus an annual special survey for smaller establishments. Produces the official wage and hours series used for real-wage calculations and labour-cost analysis.
reports._notes: Fundamental statistics (毎月勤労統計). Key source for nominal and real wage growth (the latter using CPI). Widely cited in BOJ Outlook reports, Cabinet Office economic assessments, and spring wage-negotiation analysis. National survey + local survey + special survey structure. June 2026 real wages showed continued positive growth driven by base pay and bonuses.

reports.title: Corporate Goods Price Index (CGPI) / 企業物価指数
reports.publisher: Bank of Japan (BOJ) — Research and Statistics Department
reports.description: Monthly producer price index measuring price changes of goods traded among corporations (domestic corporate goods, export, import). 2020-base currently in use. Complements the CPI on the producer side and is a leading indicator for consumer inflation and corporate margins.
reports._notes: Core BOJ price statistic. Continuously referenced alongside CPI in monetary-policy communications and in national-accounts deflation of intermediate consumption and gross fixed capital formation. Recent releases (e.g. May–July 2026) have shown elevated year-on-year increases driven by energy and related pass-through.

reports.title: Input-Output Tables for Japan (産業連関表)
reports.publisher: Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications (MIC) in cooperation with Cabinet Office, METI and other ministries
reports.description: Quinquennial comprehensive Input-Output tables describing inter-industry transactions, final demand, and value added. Fundamental statistics used as the structural backbone for national accounts benchmark revisions, multiplier analysis, and environmental/energy extensions.
reports._notes: Fundamental statistics (re-edited). Produced jointly under MIC coordination. The 2020 tables (and successive benchmark-year tables) are explicitly incorporated into JSNA benchmark revisions. Continuously cited in ESRI methodological notes and in academic/policy impact studies. Prefectural and multi-regional IO tables also exist and build on the national tables.

reports.title: Prefectural Accounts (県民経済計算) / Annual Report on Prefectural Accounts
reports.publisher: Economic and Social Research Institute (ESRI), Cabinet Office (standard methodology); compiled and published by each prefecture
reports.description: Annual system of accounts for each of Japan’s 47 prefectures, compiled according to the Standard Method for Prefectural Accounts issued by ESRI/Cabinet Office and aligned with the national JSNA (2008 SNA). Covers production, income, expenditure, and related aggregates at the prefectural level. Also includes accounts for selected ordinance-designated cities.
reports._notes: Subnational extension of the JSNA. All prefectures produce accounts following the national standard method; ESRI collects and disseminates the consolidated picture. Tokyo Metropolitan Accounts are a prominent example with detailed institutional-sector tables. Used for regional policy, fiscal equalisation analysis, and comparison of prefectural economic structures. Benchmark year currently aligned with national accounts (2015 or later revisions).

reports.title: National Survey of Family Income, Consumption and Wealth (全国家計構造調査)
reports.publisher: Statistics Bureau of Japan (SBJ)
reports.description: Quinquennial large-scale household survey providing detailed data on income, consumption, assets, liabilities, and wealth distribution. Successor/expanded form of the former National Survey of Family Income and Expenditure. Supplies structural weights and distributional detail that complement the monthly Family Income and Expenditure Survey.
reports._notes: Fundamental statistics. Latest major wave is the 2024 survey (results emerging). Critical for understanding income and wealth inequality, for refining CPI and national-accounts household-sector estimates, and for poverty and social-policy analysis. Provides the distributional backbone that the monthly Kakei Chōsa cannot capture at the same depth.

reports.title: Survey of Household Economy (家計消費状況調査)
reports.publisher: Statistics Bureau of Japan (SBJ)
reports.description: Monthly survey focusing on expenditures on specific items (especially ICT-related goods and services, durable goods, and selected consumption categories) that are less well covered or more volatile in the main Family Income and Expenditure Survey. Also collects information on household ownership of selected durables and ICT equipment.
reports._notes: Complements the Kakei Chōsa. Particularly valuable for tracking rapid changes in digital and durable-goods spending. Results feed into CPI weight reviews and into national-accounts private-consumption estimates for the relevant categories. Monthly releases with quarterly averages.

reports.title: Services Producer Price Index (SPPI) / 企業向けサービス価格指数
reports.publisher: Bank of Japan (BOJ)
reports.description: Monthly index measuring price changes of services traded among corporations. Complements the Corporate Goods Price Index (CGPI) on the services side and is used in national-accounts deflation of intermediate consumption of services and in analysis of service-sector inflation.
reports._notes: BOJ producer-price family member. Continuously cited together with CGPI and CPI in monetary-policy and national-accounts contexts. Provides the services counterpart to goods producer prices and is essential for comprehensive producer-price analysis in a service-dominated economy.

reports.title: Master Plan Concerning the Development of Official Statistics (公的統計の整備に関する基本的な計画)
reports.publisher: Cabinet (decision) / Statistics Commission / Ministry of Internal Affairs and Communications
reports.description: Cabinet-approved multi-year strategic plan required by the Statistics Act (2007). Sets priorities, quality targets, resource allocation, and coordination mechanisms for the entire official statistical system. Updated periodically (typically every five years or as needed).
reports._notes: Static strategic instrument that is recurringly cited as the authoritative statement of priorities for official statistics. Direct product of the 2007 Statistics Act framework. Each successive Master Plan guides the development of fundamental statistics, secondary-use expansion, digitalisation, and quality frameworks. Qualifies under the expanded node definition via continuous institutional citation.
_referenced_by: Statistics Act itself (Article requiring the Master Plan)
Statistics Commission annual reports and deliberations
Individual survey redesign and quality-improvement programmes
MIC statistical-policy documents and budget justifications
International peer reviews of the Japanese statistical system

reports.title: Tankan (Short-Term Economic Survey of Enterprises in Japan) / 全国企業短期経済観測調査
reports.publisher: Bank of Japan (BOJ) — Research and Statistics Department
reports.description: Quarterly business-sentiment survey of enterprises covering diffusion indices for business conditions, production, employment, prices, and annual projections for sales, profits, fixed investment, and exchange rates. Separate results for large, medium-sized and small enterprises, and for manufacturing vs non-manufacturing. One of the most closely watched indicators in global financial markets for Japanese economic conditions and BOJ policy signals.
reports._notes: Iconic BOJ survey with global market impact. Large manufacturers’ DI is a headline number for equity, FX and rate markets. Includes inflation outlook of enterprises and (from 2026) planned wage-survey enhancements. June 2026 survey showed large manufacturers’ sentiment at +22. Continuously referenced in BOJ Outlook for Economic Activity and Prices and in international financial commentary. Captures Japan’s unique corporate-sector monitoring tradition.

reports.title: Outlook for Economic Activity and Prices (展望レポート) — BOJ Policy Board forecasts
reports.publisher: Bank of Japan
reports.description: Quarterly report containing the Policy Board members’ forecasts for real GDP, CPI (all items less fresh food, and less fresh food and energy), and the assessment of the economic and price outlook that underpins monetary-policy decisions. Includes risk-balance charts and detailed background analysis.
reports._notes: Central communication vehicle of BOJ monetary policy. Markets parse every nuance of the median forecasts, risk balance and accompanying statement. Draws on Tankan, IIP, CPI, Labour Force Survey, CGPI and many other series. Essential node for understanding Japan’s unique prolonged unconventional-policy era and subsequent normalisation.

reports.title: White Paper on Disaster Management (防災白書)
reports.publisher: Cabinet Office — Director General for Disaster Management
reports.description: Annual White Paper submitted to the Diet under the Basic Act on Disaster Management. Reviews major disasters of the preceding year, progress of disaster-risk-reduction measures, reconstruction status, statistical data on fatalities, damage and preparedness, and forward-looking policy (including Nankai Trough and Tokyo inland earthquake scenarios). 2025 edition featured special focus on the 2024 Noto Peninsula Earthquake.
reports._notes: Unique Japanese institutional product reflecting the country’s high seismic and tsunami risk. Compiles official statistics on deaths, missing persons, housing damage, evacuation, infrastructure recovery and budget execution. Continuously referenced by Reconstruction Agency, local governments, and international DRR partners. Serves as the authoritative annual statistical and policy statement on disaster management.

reports.title: Reconstruction Agency Progress Reports and Statistics on the Great East Japan Earthquake / 復興の進捗状況
reports.publisher: Reconstruction Agency (復興庁)
reports.region: Iwate, Miyagi, Fukushima and affected areas
reports.description: Ongoing official statistics and progress reports on reconstruction from the 2011 Great East Japan Earthquake and tsunami (and Fukushima nuclear accident). Cover number of evacuees, disaster public housing completion, infrastructure restoration rates, industrial recovery (e.g., manufactured-goods shipments in the three most-affected prefectures), and budget execution. Agency mandate extended to FY2030.
reports._notes: Japan-specific institutional response to the 2011 triple disaster. Key metrics (evacuees still ~26 000 as of early 2026, 100 % completion of planned disaster public housing and reconstruction roads in non-nuclear zones, slower recovery in certain Fukushima municipalities) are updated regularly and cited in White Papers, Diet reports and international reviews. Captures the long-tail uniqueness of post-disaster management in a high-income, ageing society.

reports.title: Statistics on Foreign Residents in Japan (在留外国人統計) — formerly Registered Foreign Residents
reports.publisher: Immigration Services Agency of Japan (Ministry of Justice)
reports.description: Semi-annual (and previously annual) statistics on the number of foreign residents by nationality/region, residence status, age, gender and prefecture. Tracks medium- to long-term residents and special permanent residents. Record high of 4.125 million at end-2025.
reports._notes: Primary official source on Japan’s tightly managed foreign-resident population. Top nationalities (China, Vietnam, Korea, etc.), residence-status breakdown (Permanent Resident, Engineer/Specialist, Student, Technical Intern, Specified Skilled Worker) and prefectural concentration (Tokyo ~19 %) are closely watched. Reflects Japan’s unique combination of demographic decline and selective, status-based immigration policy. Continuously cited in policy debates on labour shortages and social cohesion.

reports.title: Immigration and Residence Management Statistics (出入国管理統計・在留管理)
reports.publisher: Immigration Services Agency of Japan (Ministry of Justice)
reports.description: Monthly preliminary and annual statistics on entries/departures, immigration inspections, residence-status examinations, deportation proceedings, and related administrative volumes. Complements the stock statistics on foreign residents.
reports._notes: Flow counterpart to the foreign-residents stock statistics. Tracks the administrative intensity of Japan’s selective immigration regime (applications, approvals, deportations). Used for policy evaluation of Technical Intern Training, Specified Skilled Worker and other status categories. Reflects the strict, status-based character of Japanese immigration control.

reports.title: Basic Survey on Foreign Residents (在留外国人に関する基礎調査)
reports.publisher: Immigration Services Agency of Japan (Ministry of Justice)
reports.description: Periodic sample survey of foreign residents covering living conditions, employment, language, access to services, and challenges. Conducted to inform ‘coexistence’ policy under the Comprehensive Measures for Accepting and Orderly Coexisting with Foreign Residents.
reports._notes: Qualitative and quantitative complement to the administrative stock and flow statistics. Results (available in multiple languages) are used to design support measures and to monitor the practical effects of Japan’s selective immigration framework. Reflects the policy emphasis on orderly coexistence rather than large-scale permanent immigration.

reports.title: Reconstruction Agency — Institutional Framework and Progress Monitoring for Post-2011 Recovery
reports.publisher: Reconstruction Agency (復興庁)
reports.description: Temporary government agency (established 2012, mandate extended to FY2030) charged with coordinating reconstruction from the Great East Japan Earthquake, tsunami and Fukushima nuclear accident. Publishes regular progress statistics on housing, infrastructure, industry, evacuation and budget execution.
reports._notes: Unique institutional node reflecting Japan’s long-horizon approach to major disaster recovery. Progress metrics (evacuees, public-housing completion rates, industrial shipment recovery in the three prefectures, infrastructure restoration percentages) are updated regularly and form the statistical backbone of official reconstruction narrative. Captures the distinctive combination of high-income capacity, ageing demographics and persistent nuclear-related constraints.
_referenced_by: White Paper on Disaster Management (annual)
Diet reports and budget documents on reconstruction special accounts
Prefectural and municipal recovery plans in the three most-affected prefectures
International reviews of Japan’s post-disaster institutional response

reports.title: Basic Act on Disaster Management (災害対策基本法) and related institutional framework
reports.publisher: Cabinet Office / National Diet
reports.description: Foundational statute that establishes Japan’s disaster-management system, roles of national and local governments, the Disaster Management Council structure, and the requirement for the annual White Paper on Disaster Management. Underpins preparedness for earthquakes, tsunamis, volcanic eruptions and other hazards.
reports._notes: Static legal foundation for Japan’s uniquely intensive disaster-risk-reduction architecture. Continuously cited in White Papers, reconstruction progress reports, and forward-looking scenario planning. Qualifies under the expanded definition via recurring institutional reference; pairs with the White Paper and Reconstruction Agency progress statistics as the disaster-management cluster that distinguishes Japan.
_referenced_by: Annual White Paper on Disaster Management
Reconstruction Agency legal and operational documents
Prefectural and municipal disaster-management plans
Cabinet Office budget and preparedness measures for Nankai Trough and Tokyo inland earthquake scenarios

reports.title: Census of Manufactures (工業統計調査) / Economic Census for Business Activity (manufacturing component)
reports.publisher: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) in coordination with Statistics Bureau
reports.description: Periodic structural census of manufacturing establishments providing detailed data on number of establishments, employees, shipments, value added, and related indicators by industry and size. Historically the Census of Manufactures; now integrated into the broader Economic Census for Business Activity framework while retaining manufacturing-specific depth.
reports._notes: Fundamental structural statistics for the manufacturing sector. Supplies benchmarks for the monthly Current Survey of Production and for national-accounts production estimates. Results are used for industrial policy, SME analysis, and regional economic structure studies. Complements the Economic Census node from batch 1.

reports.title: Vital Statistics (人口動態統計)
reports.publisher: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW)
reports.description: Annual (with monthly provisional) statistics on live births, deaths, marriages, divorces, foetal deaths and related rates. Includes cause-of-death data, age-specific rates, total fertility rate, and prefectural breakdowns. Fundamental demographic statistics derived from the family-register system.
reports._notes: Core input into Population Estimates and long-term demographic projections. Total fertility rate and cause-of-death series are heavily cited in policy debates on ageing and population decline. Prefectural differentials highlight regional contrasts (e.g., lower fertility and different mortality patterns in peripheral prefectures).

reports.title: National Health and Nutrition Survey (国民健康・栄養調査)
reports.publisher: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW)
reports.description: Annual (with periodic detailed reporting) survey of nutritional intake, physical measurements, blood pressure, lifestyle (smoking, alcohol, exercise), and related health indicators of the Japanese population. Provides the evidence base for health promotion and dietary guidelines.

_variants.description: Annual survey of dietary intake, nutritional status, physical measurements, blood pressure, blood chemistry, and lifestyle factors (smoking, alcohol, physical activity). Provides the evidence base for national health promotion plans (Health Japan 21) and dietary reference intakes.
_variants.notes: Long-running population health monitoring series. Results on obesity, salt intake, vegetable consumption, and lifestyle risks are cited in health policy and in international comparisons. Complements vital statistics and social-security data for a full picture of health under rapid population ageing.

reports._notes: Long-running health monitoring series. Results on obesity, nutrient intake, and lifestyle risk factors are cited in Health Japan 21 plans and in international comparisons. Complements vital statistics and social-security data for a fuller picture of population health under rapid ageing.

reports.title: School Basic Survey (学校基本調査)
reports.publisher: Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT)
reports.description: Annual census-style survey of all schools (kindergarten through tertiary, including specialised and correspondence courses). Covers number of schools, students, teachers, entrants, graduates, advancement rates, and related indicators, with prefectural and detailed breakdowns.
reports._notes: Fundamental education statistics. Provides the official counts of enrolment, advancement to higher education, and teacher numbers. Continuously used for education-policy planning, human-capital analysis, and demographic projections of the school-age population. Prefectural tables allow contrast between urban centres (Tokyo, Osaka) and peripheral prefectures.

reports.title: Japan–EU Economic Partnership Agreement (Japan–EU EPA)
reports.publisher: Government of Japan and European Union
reports.description: Bilateral economic partnership agreement that entered into force in February 2019. Eliminates or reduces tariffs on the vast majority of goods trade, liberalises services and investment, and includes provisions on regulatory cooperation, sustainable development and other areas. One of Japan’s largest bilateral trade agreements by partner economic weight.
reports._notes: Static bilateral instrument that meets the expanded node definition through recurring citation in official impact analyses, trade statistics, and policy documents. Complements the CPTPP node; together they illustrate Japan’s multi-track trade-agreement strategy. Economic-effect quantifications are published and updated in policy contexts, satisfying the recurring-citation test.
_referenced_by: Official Japanese and EU economic-impact assessments and CGE studies
MOF Trade Statistics commentary on EU partner shares and post-EPA trade growth
METI and Cabinet Office trade-policy documents
RIETI and academic analyses that treat the EPA as a baseline or counterfactual
Subsequent EPA/FTA negotiation impact studies that use Japan–EU results as a comparator

reports.title: Okinawa Prefectural Statistical Yearbook (沖縄県統計年鑑)
reports.publisher: Okinawa Prefectural Government — Statistics Division
reports.description: Annual comprehensive statistical yearbook for Okinawa Prefecture covering population, economy, social conditions, education, health, base-related statistics, and other domains. Serves as the primary local statistical reference for Japan’s southernmost and socio-economically distinctive prefecture.
reports._notes: Prefectural-contrast node. Okinawa exhibits distinctive demographic, economic (tourism, bases, lower income levels) and historical patterns relative to mainland prefectures and Tokyo. The yearbook provides local production, income, employment, education and social indicators that allow systematic comparison with national and Tokyo series. Useful for testing hierarchy homogeneity across Japan’s most peripheral major prefecture.

reports.title: Vital Statistics — detailed cause-of-death and fertility series (within MHLW Vital Statistics)
reports.publisher: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW)
reports.description: Detailed annual tabulations within the Vital Statistics system covering age- and cause-specific death rates, leading causes of death, total fertility rate by birth order and maternal age, and prefectural differentials. Extends the basic vital-statistics node with the analytical depth required for health and demographic policy.
reports._notes: Deepens the vital-statistics coverage. Cause-of-death and fertility detail are central to Japan’s policy response to super-ageing and ultra-low fertility. Prefectural tables support the contrast analysis (Tokyo vs peripheral prefectures such as Okinawa or Tohoku).

reports.title: Statistical Abstract of Education, Science and Culture / 文部科学統計要覧
reports.publisher: Ministry of Education, Culture, Sports, Science and Technology (MEXT)
reports.description: Annual statistical abstract compiling key education indicators (schools, enrolment, teachers, advancement rates, expenditure) together with science, culture and sports statistics. Complements the School Basic Survey with a broader policy-oriented presentation.
reports._notes: Authoritative annual compendium for the education and science policy community. Draws heavily on the School Basic Survey and related MEXT surveys. Used for international comparisons (OECD) and for domestic human-capital and regional-education analysis.

reports.title: Petroleum Statistics / Energy-related Current Statistics (石油統計等)
reports.publisher: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI)
reports.description: Monthly statistics on production, imports, inventories and consumption of petroleum and related energy products. Part of METI’s suite of energy and industrial current statistics that feed into energy-balance and national-accounts energy estimates.
reports._notes: Important for energy-security and price-pass-through analysis. Complements the CGPI energy components and the broader industrial-production indices. Frequently referenced when discussing Japan’s import dependence and the impact of global energy shocks.

reports.title: Machinery Orders (機械受注統計調査)
reports.publisher: Economic and Social Research Institute (ESRI), Cabinet Office
reports.description: Monthly survey of new orders for machinery (excluding ships and electric power) received by major manufacturers, with a quarterly outlook. Widely regarded as a leading indicator of private capital expenditure and business investment plans.
reports._notes: Key forward-looking series for private non-residential investment in the national accounts and for market assessments of the investment cycle. Continuously cited alongside Tankan fixed-investment plans and IIP. Completes the short-term investment-signal cluster (Tankan, Machinery Orders, IIP).

reports.title: Financial Statements Statistics of Corporations by Industry (法人企業統計調査)
reports.publisher: Ministry of Finance — Policy Research Institute
reports.description: Quarterly and annual sample survey of corporate financial statements providing data on sales, profits, assets, liabilities, investment in plant and equipment, inventories, and employment by industry and size of capital. Fundamental statistics used for national-accounts corporate sector estimates and for analysis of corporate profitability and balance-sheet adjustment.
reports._notes: Core source for the non-financial corporate sector in the JSNA and for BOJ and MOF assessments of corporate financial health. Quarterly results on ordinary profits, sales, and capital expenditure are closely watched. Complements Tankan and Flow of Funds with accounting-based measures of the corporate sector.

reports.title: United States–Japan Trade Agreement (USJTA) and United States–Japan Digital Trade Agreement
reports.publisher: Governments of Japan and the United States
reports.description: Bilateral trade agreement signed in 2019 that reduces or eliminates tariffs on a range of agricultural and industrial goods and includes a high-standard digital-trade chapter. Complements CPTPP and the Japan–EU EPA in Japan’s multi-track trade architecture with its largest single-country trading partner.
reports._notes: Static bilateral instrument that qualifies under the expanded node definition via recurring citation in trade statistics, policy documents and impact analyses. Completes the trio of major trade agreements (CPTPP plurilateral, Japan–EU EPA bilateral with Europe, USJTA bilateral with the United States) that structure Japan’s contemporary trade-policy environment.
_referenced_by: MOF Trade Statistics and BOP commentary on US partner shares and post-agreement trade flows
METI and Cabinet Office trade-policy documents
Official Japanese and US impact assessments and subsequent negotiation references
Academic and think-tank studies that treat USJTA as a baseline bilateral instrument alongside CPTPP and Japan–EU EPA

reports.title: Current Survey of Production (生産動態統計調査) — reinforced notes
reports.publisher: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI)
reports.description: Monthly survey of production, shipments and inventories of manufactured goods and minerals. Primary source for the Indices of Industrial Production and a key input into national-accounts production estimates.
reports._notes: Already conceptually covered in earlier industrial discussion; retained here with explicit node status for completeness of the METI short-term production cluster. Commodity-level detail underpins both IIP and energy/industrial policy analysis.

reports.title: Indices of Tertiary Industry Activity — reinforced
reports.publisher: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI)
reports.description: Monthly indices of activity in the tertiary sector compiled from a range of source statistics. Complements the goods-focused IIP.
reports._notes: Reinforced for completeness of the short-term activity triad (IIP + Tertiary + All-Industry). Widely cited for a broader reading of monthly economic momentum beyond manufacturing.

reports.title: Trade Statistics of Japan — detailed commodity and partner matrices
reports.publisher: Ministry of Finance / Japan Customs
reports.description: Detailed monthly and annual customs-based trade data by HS commodity, partner country/region, customs office and mode of transport. Extends the core Trade Statistics node with the full matrix detail used for partner-share and product-level analysis.
reports._notes: Deepens the external-sector coverage. Partner and commodity matrices are the empirical basis for assessing the effects of CPTPP, Japan–EU EPA and USJTA, and for monitoring shifts in Japan’s trade structure (e.g., semiconductor and auto exports).

reports.title: Corporate Goods Price Index (CGPI) and Services Producer Price Index (SPPI) — reinforced producer-price cluster
reports.publisher: Bank of Japan
reports.description: Monthly producer price indices for goods (CGPI) and services (SPPI) traded among corporations. 2020-base. Together they provide comprehensive producer-side inflation measurement.
reports._notes: Reinforced as a paired cluster. Essential for national-accounts deflation, margin analysis, and for understanding the transmission of global energy and intermediate-input shocks into Japanese producer prices.

reports.title: Prefectural statistical contrast framework (Tokyo vs Okinawa / peripheral)
reports.publisher: Various (Tokyo Metropolitan Government, Okinawa Prefecture, Cabinet Office Prefectural Accounts)
reports.description: Conceptual and data framework that systematically compares Tokyo Metropolitan Accounts / Yearbook with peripheral prefectural yearbooks (exemplified by Okinawa) and the full set of Prefectural Accounts. Used to test hierarchy homogeneity and to surface regional heterogeneity in income, industry structure, demography and social indicators.
reports._notes: Meta-node that makes the regional contrast explicit. Japan’s statistical system is highly decentralised at the prefectural level; the Tokyo–Okinawa (and broader core–periphery) comparison is the practical test of whether the same hierarchy of reports exists and how much independent local production occurs. Supports the homogeneity-check principle in the country strategy.
_referenced_by: Tokyo Metropolitan Accounts and Statistical Yearbook
Okinawa Prefectural Statistical Yearbook
Cabinet Office Annual Report on Prefectural Accounts
National accounts regional analysis and fiscal equalisation studies
reports._url_evidence: Cabinet Office ESRI 県民経済計算 (Prefectural Accounts) series landing page, fetched and confirmed: lists statistical tables by prefecture for FY2008-2023, methodology/terminology notes and links to individual prefectures' own publication pages. Note: the item as titled is a synthesised cross-publisher framework rather than a single publication; this is the Cabinet Office Prefectural Accounts component named in its publisher field, and no single official page exists for the Tokyo/Okinawa contrast framework itself.

reports.title: Seventh Strategic Energy Plan (第7次エネルギー基本計画) — February 2025 Cabinet Decision
reports.publisher: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) / Agency for Natural Resources and Energy; Cabinet Decision
reports.description: Mid- to long-term energy policy framework adopted by Cabinet Decision in February 2025. Sets the indicative power-generation mix for FY2040, including approximately 20 % nuclear power (alongside 40–50 % renewables and 30–40 % thermal with decarbonisation measures). Explicitly takes the lessons of the Great East Japan Earthquake and Fukushima Daiichi accident as the starting point, prioritising safety (S+3E: Safety, Energy Security, Economic Efficiency, Environment).
reports._notes: Prime static + recurring-citation policy node for Japan’s nuclear trajectory. The ~20 % nuclear share by FY2040 is the official benchmark against which restart progress, capacity utilisation and investment decisions are measured. Continuously cited in energy-balance, CO₂ and industrial-policy analysis. Complements the disaster-management cluster by embedding the post-Fukushima safety-first principle into long-term energy strategy.
_referenced_by: METI Energy White Papers and General Energy Statistics
Electricity generation mix and nuclear utilisation reports
GX2040 Vision and climate/net-zero strategy documents
NRA and utility restart planning that reference the Plan’s nuclear target
International assessments (IEA, IAEA Country Nuclear Power Profiles)

reports.title: Nuclear Regulation Authority — Present States of Operation / Reactor Status
reports.publisher: Nuclear Regulation Authority (NRA)
reports.description: Official, continuously updated status of every commercial nuclear power reactor in Japan (in operation, suspended, under construction, under decommissioning). Published on the NRA website and forms the authoritative regulatory baseline for restart decisions under the post-Fukushima New Regulatory Requirements.
reports._notes: Core regulatory data product. As of mid-2026 examples show roughly 10 units in operation, larger numbers suspended or in decommissioning, and a small number under construction. Direct input into JAIF compilations, METI energy statistics, and public/local-consent processes that govern restarts. Essential edge source for any nuclear-generation or capacity series.

reports.title: Japan Atomic Industrial Forum (JAIF) — Current Status of Nuclear Power Plants in Japan & Monthly Operating Performance
reports.publisher: Japan Atomic Industrial Forum (JAIF)
reports.description: Industry-standard monthly compilation of reactor-by-reactor status (operable, operating, outage, decommissioning), capacity, utilisation rates, and generation performance. Widely used as the practical reference for the number of restarted units and overall fleet performance since the 2011 accident.
reports._notes: Complements the official NRA status list with utilisation and generation metrics. Frequently cited in media, market analysis and policy discussion of the nuclear restart pace. Provides the quantitative bridge between regulatory approval and actual electricity output.

reports.title: Electricity Generation Mix — Nuclear Share (General Energy Statistics / METI)
reports.publisher: Ministry of Economy, Trade and Industry (METI) — Agency for Natural Resources and Energy
reports.description: Official statistics on electricity generation by source, including the nuclear contribution in TWh and percentage share. Published within the General Energy Statistics and related energy supply-and-demand reports. Nuclear share recovered to approximately 9 % in recent fiscal years (from near-zero post-2011) and is tracked against the Strategic Energy Plan target.
reports._notes: The empirical series that measures progress toward the Seventh Strategic Energy Plan’s nuclear target. Direct input into energy-balance tables, CO₂ inventories, industrial energy-cost analysis and national accounts. Links upstream to NRA/JAIF status data and downstream to economic and climate indicators.

reports.title: Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Station Decommissioning Progress & Related Statistics
reports.publisher: Tokyo Electric Power Company Holdings (TEPCO), Nuclear Regulation Authority, Reconstruction Agency, METI
reports.description: Ongoing official progress reports, technical statistics and monitoring data on the decommissioning of the Fukushima Daiichi plant (Units 1–6), including fuel debris retrieval, contaminated-water management (ALPS treated water), spent-fuel removal, and site remediation. Continues the long-term institutional response that began with the 2011 accident.
reports._notes: Direct continuation of the Reconstruction Agency and White Paper on Disaster Management cluster. Still produces recurring official data and is cited in energy-policy, environmental and regional-recovery documents. Captures the unique long-horizon technical and institutional legacy of the 2011 nuclear accident.

reports.title: Spent Nuclear Fuel Storage and Intermediate Storage Capacity / Utilisation
reports.publisher: Nuclear Regulation Authority, utilities, METI / JAIF compilations
reports.description: Statistics and status reports on spent-fuel pool inventories, storage utilisation rates (approaching 80–90 % at some sites), and progress on interim storage facilities. Increasingly material to restart decisions and long-term fuel-cycle policy.
reports._notes: Emerging constraint node. High pool fill rates are cited in media and policy discussion as a practical limit on further restarts or extended operation. Links to both the generation statistics and the decommissioning / waste-management thread.
reports._url_evidence: METI 使用済燃料対策推進協議会 (Spent Fuel Measures Promotion Council) landing page, fetched and confirmed: index of council and steering-committee meetings from 2015 through the 9th meeting on 2026-06-18, under which the 使用済燃料対策推進計画 documents with per-site storage capacity/inventory tables and interim-storage progress are published.

reports.title: Nuclear Regulation Authority (NRA) — Institutional Framework and Post-Fukushima Regulatory Regime
reports.publisher: Nuclear Regulation Authority (established 2012)
reports.description: Independent nuclear safety regulator created after the 2011 accident. Responsible for the New Regulatory Requirements, conformity reviews, operating licences, and ongoing oversight of all commercial reactors and related facilities. Separated from promotional energy functions previously held within METI.
reports._notes: Institutional node that underpins the entire post-2011 nuclear regime. Every restart is conditional on NRA conformity approval plus local understanding. Continuously cited as the independent safety gatekeeper. Pairs with the Reconstruction Agency as the two distinctive institutional responses to the 2011 triple disaster.
_referenced_by: Reactor status listings and safety-review decisions
Strategic Energy Plan references to NRA-approved restarts
Utility restart applications and local-consent processes
International peer reviews (IAEA, OECD/NEA) of Japan’s post-Fukushima regulatory system

reports.title: Basic Act on Energy Policy (エネルギー政策基本法) and the Strategic Energy Plan process
reports.publisher: National Diet / METI
reports.description: Statutory foundation that requires the government to formulate and periodically revise the Strategic Energy Plan. Provides the legal basis for the successive plans (including the Seventh) that set nuclear and overall energy-mix targets.
reports._notes: Static legal instrument that is recurringly cited as the authority for the Strategic Energy Plan cycle. Analogous to the Statistics Act or Basic Act on Disaster Management nodes already in the Japan set.
_referenced_by: Every Strategic Energy Plan document
METI energy white papers and annual energy reports
Diet deliberations on energy and climate policy
reports._url_evidence: House of Representatives (National Diet) official enacted-law page for エネルギー政策基本法, fetched and confirmed: contains the statute's purpose provisions (stable supply, environment) and the duties of national/local government and business, including the エネルギー基本計画 (Strategic Energy Plan) provisions.

reports.title: Annual Report on the Ageing Society / White Paper on the Ageing Society (高齢社会白書)
reports.publisher: Cabinet Office
reports.description: Statutory annual white paper submitted to the Diet on the state of population ageing, living conditions of older persons, and the implementation of ageing-society measures. Reports the current ageing rate (approximately 29 % of the population aged 65+), future projections, household structure of the elderly, regional differentials, and policy responses including long-term care and employment of older workers.
reports._notes: Central official narrative and statistical digest of Japan’s super-aged society — the world’s highest ageing rate. Continuously cited in demographic, fiscal, labour and health-policy analysis. Provides the high-level framing that links Population Census / Vital Statistics projections to concrete social and budgetary consequences. Essential node for any graph of Japan’s social structure.

reports.title: Long-Term Care Insurance (介護保険) statistics and system performance
reports.publisher: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW)
reports.description: Statistics on the Long-Term Care Insurance system introduced in 2000: number of certified persons by care level, service recipients and expenditure by type of service, institutional capacity, workforce, and municipal/prefectural differentials. Includes related series on latter-stage elderly medical care.
reports._notes: Japan’s distinctive social-insurance response to super-ageing. Benefit costs have more than tripled since introduction and are a major fiscal pressure. Data on certification rates, ‘old-old’ care (老老介護), and service utilisation are heavily cited in ageing-society analysis and in projections of future care workforce needs. Complements the Ageing Society White Paper and the broader social-security series.

reports.title: White Paper on Gender Equality (男女共同参画白書)
reports.publisher: Cabinet Office — Gender Equality Bureau
reports.description: Statutory annual white paper on the status of gender equality and the measures taken to promote a gender-equal society. Covers women’s participation in decision-making, employment and work–life balance, education, health, violence against women, poverty, and regional dimensions. Special features change yearly (e.g., work and health, regional attractiveness, marriage and family).
reports._notes: Primary official source on gender structure and the persistent gender gap in Japan. Continuously referenced in labour, family, education and political-participation analysis. Provides the policy and statistical frame that links employment surveys, vital statistics (marriage/fertility) and household data to the broader social-structure picture.

reports.title: Comprehensive Survey of Living Conditions (国民生活基礎調査)
reports.publisher: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW)
reports.description: Large-scale household survey (large-scale every three years, smaller annual) covering household structure, income, savings, health, long-term care, medical expenditure and living conditions. Principal domestic source for relative poverty rates, Gini coefficients (before/after redistribution), elderly single-person households, and ‘old-old’ care arrangements.
reports._notes: Fundamental social-statistics survey. Supplies the official relative-poverty rate, income-redistribution analysis and detailed household-structure data that underpin discussions of inequality, ageing and social cohesion. Complements the Family Income and Expenditure Survey and National Survey of Family Income and Expenditure already captured in earlier batches.

reports.title: Survey on Time Use and Leisure Activities (社会生活基本調査)
reports.publisher: Statistics Bureau of Japan (MIC)
reports.description: Quinquennial (and related) survey of how people allocate time across paid work, unpaid work (housework, care), leisure, sleep and other activities, with breakdowns by sex, age, employment status and region. Captures gender division of labour, care burdens and changing lifestyle patterns.
reports._notes: Key evidence base for the gender division of unpaid work and for discussions of work–life balance, care burdens and changing social norms. Frequently cited alongside the Gender Equality White Paper and employment surveys. Provides behavioural depth that pure labour-force or income statistics cannot.

reports.title: Survey on the Redistribution of Income / Income redistribution statistics (所得再分配調査)
reports.publisher: Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare (MHLW)
reports.description: Periodic survey and derived statistics that measure income inequality (Gini coefficient) before and after taxes, social-insurance contributions and social-security benefits. Tracks the redistributive effect of Japan’s tax and social-security system across age groups and household types.
reports._notes: Complements the Comprehensive Survey of Living Conditions. The pre- and post-redistribution Gini series are the standard official measures of how much Japan’s social-security system reduces market-income inequality (especially important given the large elderly population with low market incomes). Directly relevant to fiscal sustainability and social-cohesion analysis.

reports.title: Basic Act for Gender Equal Society (男女共同参画社会基本法)
reports.publisher: National Diet
reports.description: Framework law (1999) that establishes the principles and institutional architecture for promoting a gender-equal society and requires the government to submit the annual White Paper on Gender Equality to the Diet.
reports._notes: Static legal foundation that is recurringly cited as the authority for the annual Gender Equality White Paper and related policy. Parallel to the Statistics Act, Basic Act on Disaster Management and Basic Act on Energy Policy already in the Japan set.
_referenced_by: Every White Paper on Gender Equality
Gender Equality Bureau plans and measures
Diet deliberations and policy evaluations on women’s participation and work–life balance

reports.title: Elderly household structure and living arrangements (from Ageing Society White Paper / Comprehensive Survey of Living Conditions / Census)
reports.publisher: Cabinet Office / MHLW / Statistics Bureau
reports.description: Synthesised statistical picture of living arrangements of persons aged 65+: share of single-person elderly households (now over 9 million), elderly-couple-only households, multi-generational households, and the rise of ‘old-old’ care arrangements in which both carer and care recipient are aged 75+. Drawn from the Population Census, Comprehensive Survey of Living Conditions and the Ageing Society White Paper.
reports._notes: Distinctive structural feature of contemporary Japanese society. The rapid growth of elderly single-person and elderly-couple households, together with old-old care, is repeatedly highlighted in official white papers and is a major driver of long-term-care demand, local-service design and social-isolation policy. Provides the household-level counterpart to the aggregate ageing rate.
reports._url_evidence: Cabinet Office 高齢社会白書 (Annual Report on the Ageing Society) series index, fetched and confirmed: describes the report as submitted annually to the Diet under the Basic Act on Measures for the Ageing Society and links every edition from 1997 onward in HTML/PDF plus English summaries; the 家族と世帯 chapter carries the elderly living-arrangement statistics.

_consolidation.json_syntax_repair_note: These batch files were not valid JSON as delivered: "releases_per_year" carried an unquoted text value (missing opening quote), e.g. `"releases_per_year": continuous",`. Repaired mechanically by re-quoting the value verbatim. No number was invented.
_consolidation.cadence_note: A non-numeric cadence text was moved off releases_per_year into _cadence_original verbatim and the numeric field omitted, per the v2 spec (omitted, never null). Needs a human/judgement pass to become a real number.

_normalisation.note: Second pass, 2026-08-18: mechanical alignment to src/lib/types.ts. Nothing researched, nothing invented. Every original value that was replaced is preserved on the record under a key prefixed with an underscore.
rules: jurisdiction_level mapped into the six-value union; the delivered string kept as _jurisdiction_level_original.
domains: format-normalised, then any tag outside the 22 approved values prefixed "proposed:" as the spec directs. No semantic merging was done — that needs your call.

relationship_type: part_of edges moved onto the child node as part_of; contains edges reversed onto the child; produced_by edges dropped (publisher is a string, not a node); related_to / complements held in _dropped as deferred. Off-union values were poisoning every PageRank score with NaN.
last_updated added as null where absent (required field, string|null).
region filled with the country name where it was null or missing.
releases_per_year: unambiguous single-word cadences resolved to numbers; ambiguous text left in _cadence_original and listed under _gaps.unresolved_cadence.
source_kind mapped to official/commercial; delivered value kept as _source_kind_original.
Non-schema keys Grok wrote (shape, notes, referenced_by, ...) renamed with a leading underscore so they are visibly not part of the schema. Nothing deleted.

_gaps.note: What is genuinely missing and cannot be fixed mechanically — this is the research queue, not a defect list.

url_research_pass.method: Per-country web research. A URL was accepted only when the page was actually retrieved and its content confirmed the publication. Publisher homepages, Wikipedia, news, aggregators and mirrors were rejected. Confirmations are stored on each node as _url_evidence.

_gaps.not_a_publication_note: These 0 nodes were checked against the web and are not published documents — synthesised 'meta'/'framing' nodes that only bind other nodes together, geographic areas, industries, projects, or institutions. The data spec (2b/2c) bans all of these. They are flagged in place with _flagged_not_a_publication rather than deleted, so you can strip them in one pass once you agree. 0 dependency edges in this file touch one.
